2834838574.name: Hukilau Beach
2834838574.description: Hukilau Beach Park is located in Lāʻie on Oʻahu.

3630742916.name: 5 Graves Beach
3630742916.description: 5 Graves Beach is off Mākena Road in South Maui near Mākena Landing Park, and is used for snorkeling and diving.
amenities: No developed restroom or shower facilities at the dive entry; nearby Makena Landing is a separate park

sources.name: PADI: Five Graves at Makena Landing

5444061201.name: Secret Beach
5444061201.description: Kauapea Beach, often called Secret Beach, is a long, secluded sandy shoreline below cliffs on Kauaʻi’s north shore near Kīlauea, distinct from military-access beaches with similar nicknames on Oʻahu.
amenities: No restrooms or showers on the sand

6047197318.name: Cromwell's Beach
6047197318.description: Cromwell’s Beach lies southeast of Diamond Head on Oʻahu. It is a generally uncrowded spot for picnicking and snorkeling.
hazards: Little beach area at high tide
Unprotected water entry and changing currents

7728877758.name: Waipū
7728877758.description: A remote, windswept stretch of wild coastline on Molokaʻi's western/southern expanse characterized by sand dunes, isolated shorelines, and rugged native brush. Highly uncommercialized and rarely visited by casual tourists; primarily a destination for rugged shoreline exploration.
hazards: High exposure to strong coastal trade winds, powerful offshore currents, and complete isolation from emergency services.

9239163584.name: Ke'ei Beach
9239163584.description: Keʻei Beach is a rocky, mostly undeveloped shoreline near Kealakekua Bay in South Kona on Hawaiʻi Island. It is not Kēʻē Beach in Hāʻena State Park, Kauaʻi.
hazards: Ocean currents and swell can change

10314397510.name: One Alii Beach Park
10314397510.description: A historic park once reserved exclusively for ancient Hawaiian royalty (Aliʻi). Features a long, flat, grassy park space and a wide, shallow sandy-bottom wading beach. Located on the southern coast just east of Kaunakakai. One of the island's designated overnight camping parks (permit required). One Aliʻi Beach Park lies on Molokaʻi’s southern shore near Kaunakakai. It is a designated camping park with shallow, rocky water.
hazards: The water is very shallow and murky, making it better suited for wading and family gatherings rather than active swimming.

10557043709.name: Kaimū Black Sand Beach
10557043709.description: Kaimū Black Sand Beach is on the changing shoreline of Kalapana, Hawaiʻi Island, with difficult access and no facilities.

11221002545.name: Swanzy Beach
11221002545.description: Swanzy Beach is in Kaʻaʻawa, Oʻahu, and is frequented for snorkeling and fishing in lower surf.
hazards: Water entry changes with tides and surf

11225437368.name: Mokulēʻia  Rock Beach
11225437368.description: A rocky, secluded coastal pocket near the Mokulēʻia coastline featuring exposed reef structures and tide pools. Frequently visited by local fishers and experienced wave explorers looking to escape crowded beach parks. Mokulēʻia Rock Beach is west of Waialua on Oʻahu. Its shaded sections attract picnickers, snorkelers and surfers.
amenities: utilizes informal roadside shoulder pull-offs along Farrington Highway
hazards: Sharp reef shelves, sudden shorebreaks, and isolated conditions with limited emergency response access.
Vehicle break-ins have been reported in parking areas

11225437369.name: Keālia Beach
11225437369.description: Keālia Beach is a sandy shoreline on northwest Oʻahu near Mokulēʻia Army Beach, west of Mokulēʻia Beach Park.
amenities: No separate developed beach-park facilities verified

11225437370.name: Mokulēʻia Beach
11225437370.description: Mokulēʻia Beach is a long stretch of sand and reef on Oʻahu's northwest shore near the Waiʻanae Mountains.
amenities: Parking and facilities at nearby Mokulēʻia Beach Park
hazards: Strong winter swell and rip currents

11293954905.name: Thukkie Beach
11293954905.description: Thukkie Beach is off Kahala Avenue and has calm water and open ocean views.
hazards: Beach access through a gated path may be closed
Little room to sit on the shore at high tide

11293954906.name: Hunakai Beach
11293954906.description: Hunakai Beach lies along Kahala Avenue and has shade and dog-friendly shore access.

11293954907.name: Waialae Beach
11293954907.description: Waiʻalae Beach in Kahala has generally calm, shallow water with a rocky bottom, near the Kahala Hotel and Waiʻalae Country Club. A footbridge connects portions of the surrounding park.

11293954908.name: Kahala Beach
11293954908.description: Kāhala Beach is a quiet, narrow south-shore beach fronting the Kāhala neighborhood east of Waikīkī.
hazards: Shallow coral reef and rocky footing

11540140829.name: Keokea Beach Park
11540140829.description: Keokea Beach Park (Boulder Beach) sits on Hawaiʻi Island’s North Kohala coast. A man-made boulder wall and natural breakwater create a calmer shallow zone, while the rocky coast attracts fishers.

12107650300.name: Polo Beach East
12107650300.description: This stretch of Polo Beach is off Farrington Highway in Waialua, Oʻahu, by the Hawaiʻi Polo Club. Sea turtles, monk seals and migrating whales may be seen offshore.
hazards: Some areas have a rocky seabed

12107674138.name: Polo Beach West
12107674138.description: This stretch of Polo Beach is off Farrington Highway in Waialua, Oʻahu, by the Hawaiʻi Polo Club. Sea turtles, monk seals and migrating whales may be seen offshore.
hazards: Some areas have a rocky seabed

12206129715.name: Turtle Bay Beach
12206129715.description: Turtle Bay is in the Kawela Bay area on Oʻahu, where beach visitors can swim and snorkel and occasionally see sea turtles.

12206151932.name: Hawaiian Electric Beach Park
12206151932.description: Hawaiian Electric Beach Park (Kahe Point) lies opposite the Kahe Generating Station. Warm-water discharge offshore attracts reef fish, turtles, eels, octopuses, and occasionally rays and dolphins.
hazards: Vehicle break-ins reported in parking area

13606879032.name: Makapu‘U Beach
13606879032.description: Makapuʻu Beach is near Sea Life Park on Oʻahu and is popular for surfing and coastal recreation.
hazards: Ocean conditions require caution around the rocky tide pools and surf

13959139639.name: Maeaea Beach
13959139639.description: Maeaea Beach is near Haleʻiwa on Oʻahu and is a location for viewing sea turtles.
hazards: Keep a respectful distance from protected sea turtles

13959139644.name: Kawailoa Beach
13959139644.description: Kawailoa Beach is the reef-fringed North Shore shoreline east of Haleʻiwa, around Puaʻena Point on Oʻahu. This record refers to the mapped beach, not a different same-named shore or distant park.

sources.name: Big Aloha Guide: Shoreline Access Facilities
Hawaiʻi DLNR — Oʻahu shoreline access locations

13961502725.name: Haleʻiwa Beach
13961502725.description: Haleʻiwa Beach on the North Shore of Oʻahu is used for swimming, surfing, fishing and turtle watching.

sources.name: Big Aloha Guide: Shoreline Access Facilities

13961502727.name: Kaiaka Bay Beach
13961502727.description: Kaiaka Bay Beach lies within the shallow, partly rocky coastline around Kaiaka Bay Beach Park west of Haleʻiwa.
amenities: Restrooms and picnic areas at nearby park

sources.name: Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

14005628515.name: Pu'uiki Beach
14005628515.description: Puʻuiki Beach is an Oʻahu North Shore beach near Waialua, between Aweoweo Beach Park and the farther-west coast. The State of Hawaiʻi identifies designated public shoreline-access routes from Waialua Beach Road; surrounding parcels should not be crossed without permission.
amenities: Designated public shoreline-access route off Waialua Beach Road (park facilities at the beach not confirmed)
hazards: Changing North Shore winter surf and currents
Stay on legal public access and do not trespass on private parcels

sources.name: Hawaiʻi DLNR — beach locations and public access (PDF)

14005628516.name: Aweoweo Beach
14005628516.description: Aweoweo Beach is a North Shore Oʻahu beach frequented for swimming, snorkeling and sea turtle watching.

14005628517.name: Makaleha Beach
14005628517.description: Makaleha Beach is a secluded beach off Kamehameha Highway in Waialua, near the polo club and local trail-riding areas.

12215433.name: Kea'au Beach Park
12215433.description: Keaʻau Beach Park lies on western Waiʻanae and has camping and picnic areas. Its rocky shelf can make water entry difficult.

12541527.name: Waimea Bay
12541527.description: Iconic North Shore destination. In summer, the bay turns crystal clear, acting like a giant natural swimming pool ideal for snorkeling, diving, and spotting sea turtles. In winter, it becomes the mecca of global big-wave surfing. Features the famous "Jumping Rock" (Da Rock) on the left side of the bay. Parking lot fills up extremely early year-round. Waimea Bay on Oʻahu’s North Shore offers clear and often calm water in summer, while winter swells can be exceptionally powerful. It is also a venue for major surfing competitions.
hazards: Lifeguarded, but winter brings massive, deadly shorebreaks and immense rip currents.
Cliff jumping off Da Rock is strongly discouraged by safety officials due to shifting shallow depths.

12541972.name: Sunset Beach
12541972.description: Sunset Beach is a North Shore beach used for fishing, surfing, and seasonal swimming. Winter surf can be very powerful.

44992151.name: Blacksand Beach
44992151.description: This black-sand beach is at Waiʻānapanapa State Park on Maui, with walking paths, scenic viewpoints and reservations required for access.

44994051.name: Red Sand Beach
44994051.description: Red Sand Beach near Hāna, Maui, is reached from the Uakea Road / Hāna Ballpark area by a short, steep coastal trail with limited street parking.
hazards: Trail is not suitable for children or people with mobility limitations

44994106.name: Hana Beach Park
44994106.description: A protected black-sand bay in the heart of Hāna town. Calm waters make it a favorite local spot for swimming, outrigger canoeing, and family gatherings. The primary community beach park of East Maui. Hāna Beach Park is in East Maui at 150 Keawa Place. It is a community beach for swimming, canoeing, fishing and other recreation; the supplied notes describe relatively mild surf.
hazards: No permanent lifeguard tower; boat traffic near the ramp, and murky water visibility after heavy rains due to stream runoff.

45054863.name: Big Beach
45054863.description: Big Beach, also called Mākena Beach or Oneloa Beach, is part of Mākena State Park on Maui.

45054906.name: Little Beach
45054906.description: Little Beach is near Puʻu Ōlaʻi within Mākena State Park, Maui.

45141928.name: Baldwin Beach
45141928.description: Baldwin Beach, also called Kapukaulua, is a long, wide sandy beach near Pāʻia, Maui. The beach is used for recreation, strolling, surfing and community activities.

sources.name: Maui County Baldwin Park Adaptation Plan

46502989.name: Hāpuna Beach State Recreation Area
46502989.description: Hāpuna Beach State Recreation Area on Hawaiʻi Island offers beach access, recreation facilities, cabins and coastal trail access.

95838103.name: Sandy Beach
95838103.description: Sandy Beach on Oʻahu is known for powerful waves breaking close to shore.
hazards: Extremely powerful shorebreak onto shallow sand

108980119.name: Hapuna Beach
108980119.description: Hāpuna Beach has coastal access to parts of the historic Ala Kahakai Trail, with a relatively sheltered northern section.

112169404.name: Kiahuna Beach
112169404.description: Kiahuna Beach in Kauaʻi’s Poʻipū area has a reef used for beginner surf lessons and snorkeling, with occasional green sea turtle sightings.
hazards: Unexpected waves can break past reef

112172088.name: Lāwaʻi Beach
112172088.description: A tiny, narrow strip of sand opening into a world-class South Shore snorkeling and scuba diving haven abundant with colorful reef fish and green sea turtles. Located in Poʻipū right across from the popular Beach House Restaurant; legendary for dramatic sunset views. Lāwaʻi Beach is a small, rocky-edged beach on Kauaʻi’s south shore, popular for reef snorkeling and access to surf breaks including PK’s, Centers and Acid Drops.
amenities: Restrooms and showers available nearby via adjacent resort/public easements
limited street parking along Lawai Road
hazards: Heavy foot traffic, slippery rocks, and strong surge near the reef wall when swells arrive.

112440148.name: Hanakapiʻai Beach
112440148.description: A stunning, remote valley-mouth beach along the Nāpali Coast framed by towering 300-foot sea cliffs and a roaring stream meeting the ocean. Accessible only by hiking the first 2 miles of the famous Kalalau Trail from Hāʻena State Park (reservations/permits required). Hanakapiʻai Beach is an isolated beach along Kauaʻi’s Nā Pali Coast, reached by a strenuous approximately four-mile round-trip hike. The trail involves uneven terrain and a stream crossing.
hazards: Notoriously dangerous: Hanakapiʻai has claimed many lives due to extreme, violent rip currents, rogue waves, and no offshore reefs to block heavy ocean swells.
Swimming or wading near the shore is strictly fatal.

112440155.name: Keʻe Beach
112440155.description: Kēʻē Beach is within Hāʻena State Park on Kauaʻi near the start of the Kalalau Trail. An offshore reef can shelter a lagoon in summer, and the beach has views of the Nā Pali Coast.
hazards: Park entry and parking require advance reservations
Remote access and restricted shuttle schedules

112440160.name: Honopū Beach
112440160.description: Honopū Beach is a remote Nā Pali Coast beach with deep Hawaiian cultural significance and a waterfall nearby. Ordinary hiking trails or boat landings do not provide permitted public access to the sand.
hazards: Access is highly restricted and hazardous

112440168.name: Kalalau Beach
112440168.description: Kalalau Beach lies along the isolated Nā Pali Coast of Kauaʻi and is associated with the 11-mile Kalalau Trail. Hiking beyond Hanakapiʻai and camping require permits.
hazards: Untreated stream water may carry disease
No lifeguards or rapid emergency response

112440704.name: Ha'ena Beach
112440704.description: Hāʻena Beach on Kauaʻi has an exposed North Shore beach and seasonal heavy surf.
hazards: Parking or entry restrictions may apply

112682438.name: Larsen's Beach
112682438.description: Larsen’s Beach on Kauaʻi is a secluded shoreline reached from a small dirt parking area by a steep, rugged dirt-and-rock footpath. It has historically been used as a clothing-optional beach.

117315648.name: Kaimana beach
117315648.description: Kaimana Beach is a sandy beach near the War Memorial Natatorium on Oʻahu, protected in part by an offshore reef. It is a launch point for swimmers and paddlers using Kapua Channel.

129264238.name: Ulua Beach
129264238.description: Ulua Beach is in Wailea, Maui, beside Mokapu Beach. Its reef system is popular for morning snorkeling and scuba diving, with frequent sea turtle sightings.
hazards: Summer south swells can produce strong shorebreak

129264843.name: Wailea Beach
129264843.description: Wailea Beach is a resort-front beach on Maui near The Shops at Wailea, with public access and substantial nearby visitor services.
hazards: Heavy activity can reduce snorkeling visibility

129264997.name: Polo Beach
129264997.description: Polo Beach is a public-access beach in Wailea, Maui, beside resorts.
hazards: Afternoon trade winds and choppy water

129576962.name: Mokapu Beach
129576962.description: Mokapu Beach in Wailea, Maui, shares a public parking area at the end of Ulua Beach Road.

129577447.name: Keawakapu Beach South
129577447.description: The south end of Keawakapu Beach in Maui has a long sandy shoreline, nearby rocky snorkeling areas and pedestrian access from resort walkways.
hazards: Strong afternoon trade winds and choppy water

129579250.name: Keawakapu Beach North
129579250.description: The north end of Keawakapu Beach on Maui is a broad sandy beach used for strolling, volleyball and shore-based winter whale watching. Offshore is a historical artificial reef site.

145181568.name: Lagoon Beach
145181568.description: Lagoon Beach is the protected, ocean-fed saltwater lagoon at Hilton Waikoloa Village in the Waikoloa resort area of Hawaiʻi Island. The sandy lagoon is used for swimming, snorkeling, and paddling; resort day passes and rental policies apply.
amenities: Lagoon beach shack and rentable watersports equipment (resort terms apply)
Paid resort day passes for non-overnight visitors
Resort cabanas and adjacent resort facilities; some services are guest-only
hazards: Snorkeling and water activities carry drowning risks even in sheltered water
Green sea turtles and other marine life inhabit the lagoon; keep a safe distance and do not touch wildlife

145181929.name: Anaehoomalu Beach
145181929.description: A wide crescent-shaped white sand beach featuring ancient Hawaiian fishponds, coconut palms, calm waters for stand-up paddleboarding, and excellent sunset views. Located within the Waikoloa Beach Resort area; rich in Hawaiian cultural history with preserved petroglyph fields nearby.
amenities: and close proximity to the Lava Lava Beach Club restaurant
hazards: Windy conditions can pick up by afternoon, creating choppy surface water.

146840623.name: Keʻehi Lagoon Beach Park
146840623.description: Large park hub along the lagoon hosting local outrigger canoe clubs, paddling, and rowing events. Located adjacent to Honolulu Harbor and the Honolulu International Airport (ideal for watching planes or local racing events).
hazards: Swimming is strongly discouraged due to water quality concerns (urban runoff/red dirt).

147229653.name: Hanauma Beach
147229653.description: Hanauma Beach lies within Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve, a protected volcanic bay on Oʻahu's southeast side known for its reef fish.
hazards: Protected marine life must not be disturbed

155871587.name: Ka'anapali Beach
155871587.description: A famous 3-mile stretch of pristine white sand and clear turquoise water. Home to Black Rock (Puʻu Kekaʻa), a premier snorkeling and sunset cliff-jumping landmark. Maui's flagship resort destination, drawing large crowds daily.
amenities: Extensive resort amenities including beachfront boardwalks
hazards: No confirmed county lifeguard tower directly on this beach; strong currents around Black Rock point, high pedestrian traffic, and boat activity offshore.

173089926.name: Kahekili Beach
173089926.description: The northern extension of Kāʻanapali. A wide, less crowded beach park featuring vibrant nearshore coral reefs packed with sea turtles and tropical fish. Named after King Kahekili; heavily favored by local snorkelers and beginner scuba divers.
hazards: Sharp coral reef right at the shoreline makes water entry tricky without reef shoes; southern end can experience exposed lava rocks during winter storms.

173108269.name: S-Turns Beach
173108269.description: S-Turns Beach, also called Pōhaku Park, is a small west Maui park along the shoreline near Kahana with views toward Molokaʻi.

173210651.name: Kapalua Beach
173210651.description: A stunning, protected, crescent-shaped golden sand bay with calm, clear water. Widely considered one of the best and safest family swimming and snorkeling spots on West Maui. Flanked by the historic Napili Kai resort structures and palm trees.
amenities: and a public parking lot (which fills up early)
hazards: Currents can pick up near the outer edges of the two flanking rock points.

173540225.name: D.T. Fleming Beach
173540225.description: A wide, golden-sand crescent beach backed by ironwood trees. Excellent for bodyboarding and sunbathing. Located in Kapalua on the northwest coast; named after a prominent pineapple company manager.
hazards: Strong shorebreaks, powerful rip currents, and high surf during winter months.

173540226.name: Oneloa Beach
173540226.description: Oneloa Beach (Ironwoods Beach) is a sandy shoreline in Kapalua, northwest Maui, near D.T. Fleming and Kapalua Beach. It is distinct from Mākena’s Big Beach, which is also sometimes called Oneloa.
hazards: Heavy winter shorebreak and rip currents

174229937.name: Kanaha Beach
174229937.description: Kanahā Beach is a long, breezy beach on Maui's north shore near Kahului Airport, known for windsurfing and kiteboarding.
amenities: Restrooms and showers at Kanahā Beach Park

179741971.name: Ala Moana Beach
179741971.description: Ala Moana Beach is a long, reef-protected urban beach beside Ala Moana Regional Park in Honolulu.

179741972.name: Magic Island lagoon
179741972.description: A man-made, seawall-enclosed protected swimming lagoon with calm, flat water, scenic skyline views of Waikīkī and Diamond Head, and a famous Friday night fireworks viewpoint. Located at the tip of the Ala Moana peninsula; extremely family-friendly.
amenities: and large parking facilities shared with Ala Moana Beach Park
hazards: Artificial concrete/rock boundaries can be slippery; ocean water exchange is limited inside the wall.

192241413.name: Haleiwa Alii Beach
192241413.description: Haleʻiwa Aliʻi Beach is a broad North Shore sandy shoreline with a reef break at Haleʻiwa Aliʻi Beach Park.

197335721.name: Kalama Beach Park
197335721.description: A quieter neighborhood extension of Kailua's main bay shoreline featuring open grassy spots and easy beach access. Popular with local residents for community recreation and peaceful beach walks.
hazards: No lifeguards on duty; strong windward chop and currents can develop.

198969264.name: Spencer Beach Park
198969264.description: A calm, protected white-sand beach sheltered from heavy open-ocean winds and waves by a massive offshore coral reef barrier. Ideal for families and young children. Rich in Hawaiian history, located near the historic Puʻukoholā Heiau National Historic Site in North Kohala.
hazards: Lifeguarded, but murky water visibility after heavy rains can occur; occasional sharp coral fragments in shallow areas.

201863713.name: Donkey Beach
201863713.description: A wide, scenic golden-sand beach on the East Shore hidden behind a canopy of ironwood trees and dense foliage. Highly private and quiet. Reached via a scenic 10-to-15-minute walk down a coastal dirt trail from the Kuhio Highway coastal path area.
hazards: Dangerous rip currents, powerful shorebreaks, and rough open-ocean waters year-round.

201863714.name: Honokohau Harbor Beach
201863714.description: A localized sandy beach pocket near the harbor entrance where green sea turtles and Hawaiian monk seals frequently haul out to rest. Located inside Kaloko-Honokōhau National Historical Park just north of Kailua-Kona.
amenities: and a nearby marina harbor store/restaurant
hazards: High volume of commercial and recreational boat traffic entering/exiting the harbor channel; swimming near the channel is restricted and unsafe.

201863716.name: Kehena Beach
201863716.description: A striking, dynamic black sand beach framed by high sea cliffs on the Puna coast; spinner dolphins are frequently spotted playing offshore. Known historically as an unofficial optional-clothing (nude) beach. Sand volume changes dramatically depending on ocean storms.
amenities: rough dirt path leads down from the coastal highway cliff edge
hazards: Extremely dangerous and unpredictable shorebreak, violent rip currents, and sudden rogue waves.

203014127.name: Makapuu Beach Park
203014127.description: Makapuʻu Beach Park is a scenic east Oʻahu beach below the Makapuʻu cliffs by Sea Life Park.

203015602.name: Lanikai Beach
203015602.description: Postcard-perfect soft white sand, calm turquoise water, and stunning views of the offshore Mokulua Islands (The Mokes). Accessed via narrow public right-of-way paths sandwiched between residential private properties in Kailua. Strict neighborhood parking restrictions apply.
hazards: Severe beach narrowing due to coastal erosion.
Strong winds and currents if venturing far offshore.

205144888.name: Hulopo‘e Beach
205144888.description: Hulopoʻe Beach is a crescent of white sand along a protected bay on Lānaʻi's south shore, next to a marine life conservation district and tide pools.

205436631.name: Mokuleia Beach Park
205436631.description: A long, remote, open sandy beach on northwestern Oʻahu near Dillingham Airfield with distant views of Kaʻena Point. Popular for wind sports, fishing, and quiet beach walks. Far removed from urban centers, giving it a rugged, isolated feel.
amenities: and water fountains. Camping is available by City and County permit
hazards: Strong winter swells, powerful rip currents, and sharp nearshore reef make swimming unsafe during high-surf periods.

205702364.name: Haleiwa Army Beach
205702364.description: A quieter coastal stretch adjacent to the broader Haleʻiwa beach park zones featuring open coastal views and local fishing spots. Historically tied to military recreation use on the North Shore.
amenities: Basic park access connected near the historic Haleʻiwa military recreation area footprint. (Shares general proximity to Haleʻiwa town infrastructure)
hazards: No dedicated full-time lifeguard tower directly on-site; strong North Shore rip currents and sharp reef structures apply.

205702365.name: Haleiwa Alii Beach Park
205702365.description: Expansive golden sand beach, sheltered western-most lifeguarded North Shore beach, great for swimming/SUP in summer and big-wave surf watching in winter. Walking distance to historic Haleʻiwa Town shops and restaurants.
hazards: Lifeguards on duty, but winter waves exceed 25 feet, generating powerful rip currents and dangerous low-tide wave breaks near the breakwater.

205783467.name: Kaiaka Bay Beach Park
205783467.description: Located on the North Shore/Waialua Bay, surrounded by coastal vegetation. Good for quiet beachcombing, picnicking, and family outings. Near the historic Waialua Sugar Mill.
amenities: and free parking spaces. Camping is available by permit
hazards: Strong currents and potential for high surf.

209294812.name: Pololu Beach
209294812.description: A dramatic, black sand and pebble beach at the mouth of the lush, sheer-cliffed Pololū Valley on the northern tip of the island. Reached via a steep, unpaved, slippery 0.6-mile switchback hiking trail descending 400 feet down the valley wall.
amenities: None at the beach level. Portable restrooms and a small viewing area are located at the lookout parking area at the top of the valley
hazards: Extreme swimming hazard: Pololū has notoriously fierce rip currents, heavy undertows, and massive river-mouth wave dynamics.
Entering the water here is extremely dangerous and often fatal.

209716687.name: Waimānalo Bay Beach Park
209716687.description: Also known locally as Sherwood Forest due to the thick canopy of towering ironwood trees lining the dunes. Wide, stunning white-sand beach with turquoise water. Frequently chosen for scenic photography and wedding backdrops.
amenities: and a shaded ironwood forest camping area (by permit)
hazards: Lifeguards on site; strong, heavy shorebreak, powerful rip currents, and Portuguese man-o'-war jellyfish arrivals following wind shifts.

210637459.name: Waialea Bay Beach Park
210637459.description: A gorgeous white-sand beach shaded by native kou and kiawe trees, offering some of the best coral reef snorkeling and fish diversity on the Kohala Coast. Famously nicknamed "Beach 69" due to an old utility telephone pole number marking the path; very popular with local families.
hazards: High surf in winter creates strong rip currents and dangerous conditions over the shallow reef.

210637461.name: Waialea Beach
210637461.description: A gorgeous white-sand beach shaded by native kou and kiawe trees, offering some of the best coral reef snorkeling and fish diversity on the Kohala Coast. Famously nicknamed "Beach 69" due to an old utility telephone pole number marking the path; very popular with local families.
hazards: High surf in winter creates strong rip currents and dangerous conditions over the shallow reef.

211228890.name: Honoli‘i Beach
211228890.description: Honoliʻi Beach, at the mouth of Honoliʻi Stream just north of Hilo, is an established surf spot with a rocky and dark-sand shoreline.

sources.name: Love Big Island Hilo Beach Guide

211397231.name: Punalu'u Black Sand Beach
211397231.description: The Big Island's most famous black basalt sand beach, widely celebrated for frequent sightings of basking endangered green sea turtles (honu) and hawksbill turtles right on the sand. Easily accessible right off the highway on the southeastern Kaʻū coast.
amenities: and a large paved parking lot
hazards: Lifeguard tower listed by Hawaiʻi Ocean Safety (confirm conditions and hours).
Federal and state laws strictly prohibit touching or getting within 10 feet of turtles.
Strong rip currents and rough open-ocean surf make swimming risky.

218679861.name: Queen Kapi'olani Beach
218679861.description: Queen Kapiʻolani Beach refers to a section of Waikīkī's shoreline adjacent to Kapiʻolani Park near Queen's Surf Beach.

218679862.name: Waikīkī Beach
218679862.description: A famous 2-mile stretch of protected, warm, gentle-sloping water divided into distinct sections (Duke Kahanamoku, Kuhio, Queen’s, Sans Souci). Perfect for learning to surf or outrigger canoeing. Oʻahu's primary tourism hub, drawing heavy crowds year-round.
amenities: Full resort-level amenities including multiple lifeguard towers
and close proximity to restaurants and hotels
hazards: Lifeguarded, but heavy crowding, box jellyfish blooms occurring 8–10 days after full moons, and deep-water channel currents/catamaran traffic exist offshore.

218680183.name: Ala Moana Beach Park
218680183.description: A 1,000-yard-long, protected swimmer's channel created by an outer fringing reef; calm, flat waters; popular for swimming, jogging, and paddleboarding. Located just west of Waikīkī within walking distance of Ala Moana Center.
amenities: children’s playground (at the Magic Island end)
hazards: The nearshore water drops off quickly; enter and exit with care.

221300288.name: White Plains Beach Park
221300288.description: White Plains Beach is a long sandy coast along the former Barbers Point military area of southwest Oʻahu, known for surf and beach walks.

228845811.name: Ko Olina
228845811.description: Four crescent-shaped, man-made, rock-barrier-enclosed lagoons providing sheltered lagoon areas that may be calmer than exposed beaches. Located on the sunny leeward (west) coast flanked by resort hotels (Aulani, Four Seasons, Marriott). Public parking fills up very early (before 8 AM).
amenities: Walking paths connecting all four man-made lagoons
and small public parking lots at each lagoon
hazards: Enclosed design means water flushes slowly; moderate bacterial risk after heavy rains (avoid swimming for 72 hours post-rain).
Slippery algae-coated rock breakwater walls present surge and slip hazards.

229240003.name: Salt Pond Beach
229240003.description: A protected, crescent-shaped golden sand beach featuring natural reef-enclosed wading pools that shield swimmers from rough open-ocean waves. Named after nearby traditional Hawaiian salt-making pans. Located on the sunny southern coast near Hanapepe; highly family-friendly.
hazards: Lifeguards on duty, but outer areas outside the protective reef experience strong currents and high surf.

229841214.name: Waiapua'a
229841214.description: A protected coastal bay and recreational area located along the western coast. Situated on the Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF) military installation grounds at Barking Sands. Access for civilians generally requires coordination, permitted base access, or MWR guest affiliation.
hazards: No lifeguards; military base operational restrictions apply, alongside standard West Side open-ocean surf and current dynamics.

229939216.name: Kekaha Beach Park
229939216.description: A long, uninterrupted stretch of golden-white sand on the sunny West Side, offering endless sunset views toward the island of Niʻihau. Popular for beachcombing and local fishing. Serves as a gateway community beach before reaching the remote stretches of Polihale State Park.
amenities: and wide shoulder parking along the highway
hazards: Lifeguard tower listed by Hawaiʻi Ocean Safety (confirm conditions and hours).
Strong, unpredictable rip currents, heavy shorebreaks, and harsh coastal winds.

230281515.name: Hāʻula Beach
230281515.description: Hāʻula Beach is a secluded stretch of coastline near the Māhāʻulepū area on Kauaʻi's south shore.

231777430.name: Mauna Kea Beach
231777430.description: Consistently ranked among America's best beaches, featuring a picturesque half-mile crescent of powdery white sand and calm, crystal-clear water. Famous for nighttime manta ray viewing offshore. Located on the Kohala Coast; strictly controlled public parking access fills up very early in the morning.
amenities: Restrooms and showers (accessed via the Mauna Kea Beach Hotel public parking system
which issues a limited number of morning visitor passes)
hazards: No official county lifeguards (though hotel resort water safety staff are present); outer bay rip currents can form during high surf.

231777910.name: Kaluhikaa Beach
231777910.description: Kaluhikaa Beach is a separately mapped stretch of coast in South Kohala on Hawaiʻi Island, about 100 metres from mapped Mauʻumae Beach and near Spencer Beach Park. Local facilities and entry conditions for this exact section are not established.

231777911.name: Mauumae Beach
231777911.description: A quiet, secluded white-sand South Kohala beach with calm, teal-colored water and lush shade trees. Far more private than neighboring major bays. Reached via a short walk from Spencer Beach Park or through a strictly limited local resort parking access trail.
amenities: None. Shares pedestrian access pathways connected to nearby coastal trails
hazards: Extremely limited official parking spots require early arrival; variable outer currents.

239375653.name: Napili Beach
239375653.description: A breathtaking, intimate crescent-shaped bay with soft white sand and crystal-clear waters. Excellent for snorkeling with sea turtles during calm summer months. Bounded by low-rise resorts and condos in West Maui.
amenities: Restrooms (located via public access rights-of-way facilities)
hazards: Winter swells bring powerful shorebreaks and strong backwash right onto the sand.

239831563.name: Mauna Lani Beach
239831563.description: Beautiful white and black sand beach pockets tucked within the Mauna Lani resort footprint, featuring calm snorkeling waters, coral reefs, and sea turtles. Accessed through gated resort community public access parking stalls with registration.
amenities: and parking lots near the resort historic pathways
hazards: Reef structures near shallow entries require cautious footing.

239951595.name: Kailua Beach Park
239951595.description: A 2.5-mile stretch of soft, white, powdery sand with brilliant turquoise water and a gentle, gradual sandy slope entry. One of Oʻahu's most popular family-friendly windward parks. Excellent launch point for kayaking.
hazards: Winds pick up significantly by midday, creating choppy surface conditions.

239951596.name: Kailua Beach
239951596.description: Kailua Beach is the long, sandy windward shore along Kailua Bay, with soft sand and open views of the Mokulua Islands.

240747547.name: Diamond Head Beach Park
240747547.description: Tucked beneath dramatic cliffs directly below the Diamond Head Crater; rugged landscape, excellent offshore surf breaks (Lighthouse, Cliffs), and tide pooling. Requires navigating a steep, rocky 80-foot paved access path/switchbacks. Frequently visited by locals and experienced surfers.
hazards: Strong currents, undertows, sharp lava rocks/coral, and hazardous shorebreaks.
Not recommended for beginners or small children.

240747548.name: Kuilei Cliffs Beach Park
240747548.description: Narrow, rocky shoreline popular with windsurfers and experienced wave riders targeting the Diamond Head Cliffs breaks. Situated directly underneath the steep coastal cliffs east of the Diamond Head Lighthouse.
amenities: Paved parking lot off Diamond Head Road and concrete access path leading down to the shore
hazards: Hazardous cliff edges, strong winds, sharp rocks, and powerful surf.

242771257.name: One‘uli Beach
242771257.description: Oneʻuli Beach is a dark, cinder-sand beach on the south side of Puʻu Olaʻi within Mākena State Park.

249472054.name: Makena Landing
249472054.description: Mākena Landing is a sheltered coastal landing area on Maui's south coast near Wailea with access to diving and kayaking waters.

261307987.name: Kamaole I Beach
261307987.description: A trio of popular golden-sand beaches in Kīhei separated by rocky points. Great for swimming, sunbathing, whale watching in winter, and seasonal boogie boarding.
amenities: All three parks feature public restrooms
and barbecue grills. Kamaʻole III features a large children's playground
hazards: Lifeguards are on duty at Kam I and Kam III (check specific towers).
Strong shorebreaks and undertows can develop during high-surf days.

261307988.name: Kamaole II Beach
261307988.description: A trio of popular golden-sand beaches in Kīhei separated by rocky points. Great for swimming, sunbathing, whale watching in winter, and seasonal boogie boarding.
amenities: All three parks feature public restrooms
and barbecue grills. Kamaʻole III features a large children's playground
hazards: Lifeguards are on duty at Kam I and Kam III (check specific towers).
Strong shorebreaks and undertows can develop during high-surf days.

261307989.name: Kamaole III Beach
261307989.description: A trio of popular golden-sand beaches in Kīhei separated by rocky points. Great for swimming, sunbathing, whale watching in winter, and seasonal boogie boarding.
amenities: All three parks feature public restrooms
and barbecue grills. Kamaʻole III features a large children's playground
hazards: Lifeguards are on duty at Kam I and Kam III (check specific towers).
Strong shorebreaks and undertows can develop during high-surf days.

287216568.name: Baby Beach
287216568.description: A shallow, calm sandy cove protected from heavy ocean surf by an outer reef barrier. Popular with families (keiki) to splash safely. Located in a residential area of Spreckelsville (near Paʻia); often confused with the West Maui baby beach in Lahaina.
hazards: Limited street parking with tight residential space; sharp coral fragments in shallow areas.

288216475.name: Slaughter House Beach
288216475.description: A stunning, pocket-sized sandy bay framed by steep sea cliffs. In summer, it offers world-class snorkeling; in winter, it transforms into an extreme wave-riding zone. Named after an old slaughterhouse that historically operated on the cliffs above.
amenities: a steep flight of concrete stairs leads down from the highway parking area
hazards: In winter, massive shorebreaks and intense rip currents make swimming fatal.
The access stairs require physical exertion to climb back up.

288995866.name: Hanamaulu Beach
288995866.description: A calm, sheltered bay beach located at the mouth of Hanamaʻulu Stream, making it protected from open-ocean wave action. Popular for local family picnics and small craft launching. Located just north of Līhuʻe near the airport corridor.
hazards: Water can become murky and turbid after heavy rain due to stream runoff, carrying bacterial runoff concerns.

289669940.name: Pebbles Beach
289669940.description: A rugged, unique coastal stretch on the Kona/South Kona coast lined entirely with smooth, dark black lava pebbles and rounded stones rather than sand. Visited primarily by local fishers, rock collectors, and travelers looking for off-the-beaten-path wave-watching spots.
hazards: Unstable footing on rolling stones; powerful shorebreaks crashing directly onto heavy boulders.

289676505.name: Magic Sands Beach
289676505.description: A popular sandy beach along Aliʻi Drive known for excellent bodyboarding waves. Named "Magic Sands" because winter storms occasionally pull all the sand off the beach overnight, exposing bare lava rock, before summer waves gradually wash the sand back ashore.
hazards: Public lifeguards serve White Sands (Laʻaloa) Beach Park; heavy, crashing shorebreaks and intense backwash frequently cause neck and shoulder injuries to swimmers and bodyboarders.

289688697.name: Makalawena Beach
289688697.description: Widely considered one of the most pristine, breathtaking white sand beaches in all of Hawaiʻi, featuring rolling sand dunes and crystal-clear water. Requires a 20-to-30-minute hike across rough, jagged ʻaʻā lava fields from Mahaiʻula Beach or Highway 19, which keeps crowds sparse.
hazards: Isolated location means emergency assistance is far away; no shade on the lava trail, and strong open-ocean currents.

289691193.name: Kua Bay Beach
289691193.description: Part of Kekaha Kai State Park, featuring brilliant turquoise blue water and dazzling white sand. Highly popular for bodyboarding and sunbathing. Easily accessible via a paved road off Highway 19 (unlike its rugged sister beaches in the park).
hazards: Can feature a powerful, heavy shorebreak and fierce backwash that easily flips bodyboarders into the sand.

289835171.name: Laupāhoehoe Beach Park
289835171.description: Laupāhoehoe Beach Park lies on a scenic, rocky point on the Hāmākua Coast with a memorial to the 1946 tsunami.

291549314.name: Kūʻau Cove
291549314.description: A tiny, picturesque cove featuring shallow tide pools and frequent visits from resting green sea turtles (honu). Tucked right next to a world-famous restaurant; popular for brief photo stops rather than extensive beach lounging.
amenities: None. Roadside gravel shoulder parking along the Hana Highway near Mama’s Fish House
hazards: Slippery rocks, sharp coral, and no formal facilities.

293644256.name: Puaena Point Beach Park
293644256.description: A scenic point just outside Haleʻiwa featuring a gentle, forgiving wave break that is widely considered one of the best spots on the North Shore for beginner surfers and longboarders. Grassy areas provide great vantage points for watching marine life like sea turtles (honu).
hazards: Lifeguards may be limited or absent depending on the exact zone; hidden rocks, sea urchins, and rip currents during high surf.

293644258.name: Haleiwa Beach Park Mauka
293644258.description: The "mauka" (mountain-side/inland) section of the park area, offering shaded trees, open green spaces, and a buffer away from the immediate sand. Frequently utilized for overflow parking, family gatherings, and shade away from direct coastal winds.
amenities: Access to standard park infrastructure shared with the broader Haleʻiwa Beach Park complex (parking
hazards: Standard park traffic and proximity to busy roadways; ocean hazards apply if heading down to the shore.

293644266.name: Haleiwa Beach Park
293644266.description: Spacious grassy lawns, large sandy area, pet-friendly environment, and a historical war memorial. Ideal for families wanting to experience the North Shore atmosphere with easier swimming access than pipeline-heavy spots.
hazards: No separate official tower for Haleʻiwa Beach Park; rocky seabed topography makes swimming hazardous during high surf or strong currents.

293645402.name: Aweoweo Beach Park
293645402.description: Aweoweo Beach is a North Shore Oʻahu beach frequented for swimming, snorkeling and sea turtle watching.

298172593.name: Baldwin Beach Park
298172593.description: Baldwin Beach, also called Kapukaulua, is a long, wide sandy beach near Pāʻia, Maui. The beach is used for recreation, strolling, surfing and community activities.

sources.name: Maui County Baldwin Park Adaptation Plan

298599505.name: Hana Beach Park
298599505.description: A protected black-sand bay in the heart of Hāna town. Calm waters make it a favorite local spot for swimming, outrigger canoeing, and family gatherings. The primary community beach park of East Maui. Hāna Beach Park is in East Maui at 150 Keawa Place. It is a community beach for swimming, canoeing, fishing and other recreation; the supplied notes describe relatively mild surf.
hazards: No permanent lifeguard tower; boat traffic near the ramp, and murky water visibility after heavy rains due to stream runoff.

298599506.name: Waikoloa Beach
298599506.description: Waikoloa Beach is a small named shoreline near Hāna Bay on East Maui, close to Waikoloa Road and Hāna Kai Maui. This is distinct from Waikoloa Beach Resort and ʻAnaehoʻomalu Bay on Hawaiʻi Island.

sources.name: Go Hawaii: ʻAnaehoʻomalu Bay (Waikoloa Beach Resort)

308376244.name: Kalepolepo Beach Park
308376244.description: Enclosed by an ancient Hawaiian fishpond (loko iʻa) rock wall, creating a shallow, waveless, warm pool that is often calmer than the open shoreline. Located in Kīhei; historically significant site for native aquaculture restoration.
hazards: The water inside the wall can become stagnant with low circulation, and the bottom is muddy/mucky rather than soft sand.

311962211.name: Kamākaʻipō Beach
311962211.description: A pristine, secluded western shore white-sand beach featuring serene turquoise waters, rugged coastal backdrops, and peaceful solitude. Located on the undeveloped West Molokaʻi coastline; typically accessed via rough coastal tracks or long walks from former ranch roads.
hazards: Isolated setting means no emergency services nearby; strong seasonal currents and unmonitored ocean conditions.

311962758.name: Kaupoa Beach
311962758.description: Consists of two stunning, twin crescent-shaped white-sand coves divided by a striking dark lava rock outcrop, featuring great tide-pooling and historic shipwreck lore (Carrier Dove, 1921). Located on the remote West Molokaʻi shore; previously the site of the Kaupoa Beach Village.
amenities: None (former resort camp structures and tentalows were permanently closed and removed)
hazards: The nearshore zone drops off quickly into deep water, and winter surf makes the coves rough and hazardous.

311963391.name: Dixie Maru
311963391.description: A small, picturesque, pocket-shaped sandy cove protected from heavy open-ocean winds and rough surf by natural rock formations. Highly popular as a calm family swimming and snorkeling spot. Located on Molokaʻi's far western tip. Named after a Japanese fishing boat (Dixie Maru) that ran aground nearby in the early 20th century.
hazards: High surf or changing seasonal swells can bypass the protective cove barrier, creating strong rip currents and undertows.

316429780.name: Chuns Reef Beach
316429780.description: A wide, sandy North Shore beach with a famous surf break suitable for various levels, a small freshwater pond for children (keiki), and tide pools. Centrally located on the "7-Mile Miracle" stretch of North Shore surf spots.
amenities: Roadside parking along Kamehameha Highway. No official indoor restrooms or showers directly on-site
hazards: Lifeguarded seasonally or part-time, but strong currents, sharp reef/rocks, and a dangerous shorebreak occur during high surf/winter months.

320314112.name: Kapukuwahine Beach
320314112.description: A secluded, rustic sand pocket situated along Molokaʻi's wild western coastline, framed by native vegetation and open coastal scenery. Part of the remote string of beaches west of Kaunakakai/Maunaloa requiring unpaved or dirt-path navigation.
hazards: Heavy winter surf, strong open-ocean currents, and total isolation from public facilities.

320314113.name: Kanalukaha Beach
320314113.description: A quiet, hidden-gem beach on the western coast near Maunaloa, offering soft sand, clear water, and a tranquil setting away from crowds. Preserves a rugged, natural environment with very low tourist traffic, serving as a peaceful place to observe marine life.
hazards: Limited cell service and remote access; variable nearshore underwater hazards and minor rock formations.

320314114.name: Papohaku Beach
320314114.description: One of the longest and widest uninterrupted expanses of pristine white sand in all of Hawaiʻi (roughly 2 miles long and 100 yards wide). Frequently completely empty of people. Located on the far west end of the island; serves as an overnight camping park (permit required).
amenities: and a parking lot at Papōhaku Beach Park
hazards: Extremely dangerous ocean conditions: Notoriously fierce rip currents, powerful shorebreaks, and heavy undertows make swimming heavily discouraged or fatal unless the ocean is dead flat and calm.

320549570.name: Kumimi Beach (20 Mile Beach)
320549570.description: Widely considered Molokaʻi's premier snorkeling and diving destination. Features a gorgeous pocket of golden sand, calm shallow waters during mid-to-high tide, and abundant marine life. Located right off the coastal highway at mile marker 20 on the East End.
hazards: Water can be extremely shallow over sharp reef shelves at low tide, requiring careful timing to avoid scraping coral.

320729396.name: Kikaua Point Beach
320729396.description: A stunning, protected, crescent-shaped white sand cove enclosed by black lava rock groins, making it a sheltered shallow-water cove on the Kohala Coast. Beautifully landscaped area with crystal-clear water and abundant marine life.
amenities: and a restricted small parking lot (requires parking passes or early arrival within the Kukio resort security framework)
hazards: Parking stalls are very limited, forcing visitors to use remote overflow lots if full.

327006283.name: Tunnels Beach
327006283.description: Widely celebrated as one of Kauaʻi's premier snorkeling and diving spots, featuring a dramatic backdrop of jagged mountain peaks, a sweeping reef system, and golden sand lined with ironwood trees. Located on the North Shore; famous windsurfing and cinematic landscape location.
amenities: highly competitive public parking lot near the access path (most visitors bike or use shuttle systems to Hāʻena areas)
hazards: Winter swells bring violent, life-threatening rip currents and breaking waves over the outer reefs; inner channels can experience swift tidal currents.

327011247.name: Nukolii Beach Park
327011247.description: A long, open stretch of coastal sand fronting the Kauai Beach Resort area, crossed by the coastal walking and biking path. Good for peaceful morning sunrises and beach walks. Rarely used for heavy recreation due to rough ocean conditions.
amenities: and a paved parking lot (connected to the beachfront resort complexes on the East Shore)
hazards: Unprotected eastern exposure means heavy surf, strong winds, and rough rip currents.

333016719.name: Maluaka Beach
333016719.description: Often called "Turtle Town," this is a wide, beautiful white-sand beach with clear water and a healthy coral reef system frequently populated by sea turtles. Quieter and less crowded than nearby Big Beach.
hazards: Strong afternoon winds can chop up the water surface and create minor currents.

333770814.name: Makena Landing Beach Park
333770814.description: A calm, sheltered bay popular as a primary launch site for scuba diving, kayaking, and stand-up paddleboarding (often seeing sea turtles and rays). Located south of Wailea; historically a busy commercial boat charter spot.
hazards: High volume of commercial kayaks, divers, and boats entering/exiting the water simultaneously.

340289519.name: Hanakao'o Beach Park
340289519.description: A long stretch of sand north of Lahaina primarily used as a hub for local outrigger canoe clubs, paddling events, and community recreation. Frequently bustling with local paddlers, picnickers, and snorkelers exploring the outer edges.
hazards: Public lifeguard tower listed by Hawaiʻi Ocean Safety.
Rocky underwater entry in places, and high vessel traffic from canoes and small watercraft.

340758318.name: VOR Beach
340758318.description: A secluded, hidden-gem beach located on Maui’s northern coastline near the airport flight path. Known for quiet sandy coves and evening visits from resident sea turtles. Reached by navigating a quiet neighborhood service road past industrial areas near Kahului.
hazards: No lifeguards; remote location with isolated parking; strong North Shore winds and unpredictable ocean currents.

340758605.name: Polo Beach
340758605.description: Polo Beach is a public-access beach in Wailea, Maui, beside resorts.
hazards: Afternoon trade winds and choppy water

358650609.name: Baby Beach
358650609.description: Baby Beach is a small reef-sheltered sandy pocket in the Poʻipū area on Kauaʻi's south shore.
hazards: Rocks and coral in shallow water

359856134.name: Hoai Bay / Lawai Beach
359856134.description: A tiny, narrow strip of sand opening into a world-class South Shore snorkeling and scuba diving haven abundant with colorful reef fish and green sea turtles. Located in Poʻipū right across from the popular Beach House Restaurant; legendary for dramatic sunset views.
amenities: Restrooms and showers available nearby via adjacent resort/public easements
limited street parking along Lawai Road
hazards: Heavy foot traffic, slippery rocks, and strong surge near the reef wall when swells arrive.

359856164.name: Lawai Beach
359856164.description: A tiny, narrow strip of sand opening into a world-class South Shore snorkeling and scuba diving haven abundant with colorful reef fish and green sea turtles. Located in Poʻipū right across from the popular Beach House Restaurant; legendary for dramatic sunset views.
amenities: Restrooms and showers available nearby via adjacent resort/public easements
limited street parking along Lawai Road
hazards: Heavy foot traffic, slippery rocks, and strong surge near the reef wall when swells arrive.

360100820.name: Polihua Beach
360100820.description: Polihua Beach is a remote, wide sandy beach on the north coast of Lānaʻi. Visitors use the shoreline for beachcombing, sunbathing and coastal wildlife viewing; its exposed water is not suitable for swimming.
amenities: No public restrooms, showers or other developed facilities
hazards: Dangerous ocean currents and strong surf; do not swim

364793525.name: Kūhiō Beach
364793525.description: This Kūhiō Beach is a sandy shoreline on Hawaiʻi Island beside Kukiʻo Bay and Kikaua Point, south of the Four Seasons Resort Hualālai area. It is NOT the Waikīkī Kūhiō Beach on Oʻahu.
amenities: Designated shoreline-access routes within the Kukiʻo/Hualālai area
Nearby public-access parking and restrooms are available at specified shoreline access points; not confirmed directly on the sand
hazards: Rocky or uneven lava shoreline sections
Surf and currents vary with swell
Access and parking may be limited to designated public shoreline-access areas

sources.name: Hawaiʻi County Planning — North Kona shoreline access

366072005.name: Three Tables
366072005.description: Named after three flat, table-like reef formations just offshore. In summer, it transforms into an exceptional, clear-water snorkeling and diving sanctuary within the Pupukea Marine Life Conservation District. Located right on the North Shore between Sharks Cove and Waimea Bay.
amenities: Relies on nearby Pupukea Beach Park infrastructure (restrooms
showers across the highway near Sharks Cove)
hazards: No lifeguard tower verified directly on Three Tables; winter brings massive, highly dangerous surf (>20 ft) with intense structural rip currents over the shallow reef.

380432646.name: Pakala Beach
380432646.description: A legendary West Side surf spot known for "Infinities," a remarkably long, peeling left-hand wave breaking over an outer reef. Located in the Pakala/Waimea region; primarily utilized by experienced local surfers and boaters.
amenities: None. Remote shoreline access with informal dirt shoulder parking
hazards: Sharp shallow coral reef, strong offshore currents, and private property boundaries surrounding inland access paths.

380702914.name: Hāʻena Beach Park
380702914.description: Hāʻena Beach Park fronts the north shore beneath the green mountains and near Makana (Bali Hai).

386560909.name: 'Ai'ōpio Beach
386560909.description: ʻAiʻōpio Beach is a coastal area within Kaloko-Honokōhau National Historical Park, near protected fishponds and historic shoreline sites.

386560910.name: Kaelehuluhulu Beach
386560910.description: A remote, scenic white sand beach situated inside Kekaha Kai State Park, bordered by ancient lava flows and native coastal vegetation. Reached via a roughly 2-mile unpaved, bumpy access road off Highway 19; gates lock at sunset.
amenities: and a designated dirt parking lot
hazards: Strong shorebreaks, unpredictable rip currents, and sharp underwater lava rocks.

386560911.name: Mahaiula Beach
386560911.description: A gorgeous, remote white sand crescent framed by black lava fields and kiawe trees. Very peaceful atmosphere. Accessed via a rugged, unpaved 1.5-mile lava road requiring high-clearance vehicles, or via a scenic coastal walking trail.
amenities: Pit toilets/portable restrooms near the northern edge of Kekaha Kai State Park
hazards: Intense afternoon heat, sharp lava rocks, and strong unmonitored ocean currents.

386560912.name: Makolea Beach
386560912.description: A hidden coastal pocket south of Kailua-Kona featuring ancient heiaus (temples), petroglyphs, and sheltered tide pools good for light wading. Maintained primarily as a cultural shoreline access point rather than a traditional sunbathing beach.
amenities: None. A paved accessible pathway leads from Aliʻi Drive down through historic cultural sites
hazards: Sharp volcanic rock shelves and rough wave impacts make swimming unsafe.

389298446.name: Kapaa Beach Park
389298446.description: Kapaʻa Beach Park is a shoreline park in Kapaʻa town on Kauaʻi's east coast.

389940955.name: Kalapaki Beach
389940955.description: A wide, crescent-shaped, wave-protected golden-sand bay that serves as a hub for swimming, stand-up paddleboarding, and outrigger canoe paddling. Located in Līhuʻe, fronting Nawiliwili Bay where commercial cruise ships sometimes dock.
amenities: Full resort facilities available via the adjacent Marriott Kauai Beach Club
hazards: No county lifeguards (though hotel resort security/water safety presence exists); occasional boat traffic near the harbor mouth.

413420356.name: Waimanalo Beach
413420356.description: Waimānalo Beach extends along Oʻahu's windward coast with broad soft sand, ironwood trees and views of the Koʻolau Range.
amenities: Restrooms and showers at beach park

415221480.name: Honokowai Beach Park
415221480.description: A narrow, park-lined coastal strip with a shallow, reef-protected pool that breaks most incoming waves, making it popular for toddlers. Located just north of Lahaina in a densely populated condo area.
hazards: The water can be murky and rocky, and the beach is often heavily littered with washed-up seaweed/coral rubble.

441540468.name: Kapahukapu (Manini Beach)
441540468.description: A serene, historic community beach park on Kealakekua Bay featuring shade trees and a rocky/sandy mix entry. Great spot for launching kayaks or paddleboards across the bay to the Cook Monument (permits/rules apply). Located in Captain Cook; steeped in deep Hawaiian historical significance.
amenities: and a small area for parking along Manini Beach Road
hazards: Strong currents in the deep middle of Kealakekua Bay if paddling far out.

441801193.name: Ke'ei Beach
441801193.description: Keʻei Beach is a rocky, mostly undeveloped shoreline near Kealakekua Bay in South Kona on Hawaiʻi Island. It is not Kēʻē Beach in Hāʻena State Park, Kauaʻi.
hazards: Ocean currents and swell can change

443107867.name: Kōkī Beach
443107867.description: A striking red-sand beach near Hāna created by the erosion of the nearby iron-rich red cinder cone (Kaʻuiki). Wild, rugged scenery. Deeply tied to Hawaiian mythology as the birthplace of Queen Kaʻahumanu.
amenities: and a small dirt parking area off the Hāna Highway
hazards: Extremely dangerous and powerful shorebreak, heavy rip currents, and razor-sharp underwater rocks.

443107869.name: Hamoa beach
443107869.description: A gorgeous, crescent-shaped greyish-white sand beach framed by lush green sea cliffs on the road past Hāna. Outstanding for body surfing. Managed partially by a nearby resort, but open to the public; accessed via a staircase from the road.
amenities: and a small parking area along the upper roadway
hazards: No verified regular public tower; powerful shorebreaks, rip currents, and strong undertows are common, especially with changing swells.

447039755.name: Sugar Beach
447039755.description: A multi-mile, uninterrupted stretch of flat, sandy coastline running along Keālia Pond National Wildlife Refuge. Ideal for long, peaceful beach walks. Named after the historic Maui sugar shipping operations that once used the nearby coast.
amenities: Restrooms and showers at specific public access points (such as Kihei Canoe Club or North Kihei road accesses)
hazards: Highly exposed to strong trade winds (making it very windy by midday); occasional Portuguese man-o'‑war wash-ups.

447933474.name: Kihei Beach Reserve / Waipuilani Park
447933474.description: Waipuʻilani Beach fronts several condominiums on South Kīhei Road, Maui. It has a long sand-and-coral shoreline with an offshore reef and sunset views.
hazards: Coral and reef along the shoreline

449434261.name: Keawakapu I Beach Park
449434261.description: Keawakapu I Beach Park provides public access to the north section of Keawakapu Beach in South Kīhei, Maui.

449437360.name: Keawakapu II Beach Park
449437360.description: Keawakapu II Beach Park is a public access point along Keawakapu Beach near the Kīhei–Wailea boundary.

449443874.name: Ulua Beach Park
449443874.description: Ulua Beach is in Wailea, Maui, beside Mokapu Beach. Its reef system is popular for morning snorkeling and scuba diving, with frequent sea turtle sightings.
hazards: Summer south swells can produce strong shorebreak

449721272.name: Wailea Beach
449721272.description: Wailea Beach is a resort-front beach on Maui near The Shops at Wailea, with public access and substantial nearby visitor services.
hazards: Heavy activity can reduce snorkeling visibility

450385894.name: Kamaole Beach Park
450385894.description: A trio of popular golden-sand beaches in Kīhei separated by rocky points. Great for swimming, sunbathing, whale watching in winter, and seasonal boogie boarding.
amenities: All three parks feature public restrooms
and barbecue grills. Kamaʻole III features a large children's playground
hazards: Lifeguards are on duty at Kam I and Kam III (check specific towers).
Strong shorebreaks and undertows can develop during high-surf days.

451656342.name: Palauea Beach
451656342.description: Palauea Beach, also called White Rock Beach, is a quieter sandy stretch between Wailea and Mākena on South Maui.

451656343.name: Polo Beach Park
451656343.description: Polo Beach is a public-access beach in Wailea, Maui, beside resorts.
hazards: Afternoon trade winds and choppy water

451683154.name: Ka'opala Beach
451683154.description: Kaʻopala Beach is a small sandy shoreline segment in the Kahana–Nāpili area of West Maui.

451683155.name: Keka'a Beach
451683155.description: Kekaʻa Beach is part of the West Maui shoreline near the northern end of Kāʻanapali, with sand and rocky reef.

451683156.name: Keonenui Beach
451683156.description: Keonenui Beach is a quiet, narrow beach in the Kahana area of West Maui, fronting residential and resort properties.

451683157.name: Punalau Beach
451683157.description: Punalau Beach is a small West Maui coastal beach, sometimes called Windmills, on the northwestern shoreline.

451759382.name: Chang's Beach
451759382.description: Chang's Beach is a sandy, scenic section of Pōʻōlenalena Beach Park in Mākena, South Maui.

451759384.name: Po'olenalena Beach
451759384.description: Pōʻōlenalena Beach is a broad sandy South Maui beach between Wailea and Mākena, also linked with Chang's Beach.

451759385.name: Po'Olenalena Beach
451759385.description: Pōʻōlenalena Beach is a sandy, less developed stretch of the South Maui shoreline with offshore views toward Kahoʻolawe.

456490970.name: Hookipa Park Beach
456490970.description: Hoʻokipa Beach Park is a well-known surf and windsurfing location on Maui's north shore along Hāna Highway.

461622569.name: Kolekole Beach Park
461622569.description: Kolekole Beach Park is a coastal park at the mouth of Kolekole Stream along the Hāmākua Coast north of Hilo.
hazards: Rocky entry and strong ocean surf

461625170.name: Kealoha Beach Park
461625170.description: James Kealoha Beach Park, sometimes called Four Mile Beach, is a rocky, tide-pool shoreline in Hilo's Keaukaha area.

461626901.name: Richardson Beach Park
461626901.description: Richardson Ocean Park has a small dark-sand and lava-rock coastline in Hilo, with sheltered coves used for snorkeling.

sources.name: Love Big Island Hilo Beach Guide

461626902.name: Waiuli Beach Park
461626902.description: Waiuli Beach Park, also called Leleiwi Beach Park, contains rocky coves and natural pools along Hilo's coast.
hazards: Surf and currents beyond protected coves

sources.name: Love Big Island Hilo Beach Guide

461626903.name: Waiolena Beach Park
461626903.description: Waiolena Beach Park is a small coastal park within Hilo's Keaukaha shoreline of lava-rock inlets and coastal pools.

461626904.name: Onekahakaha Beach Park
461626904.description: Onekahakaha Beach Park is a shallow, reef-protected tidal pool and family beach park near Hilo Airport.

461638553.name: Reeds Bay Beach Park
461638553.description: Reeds Bay Beach Park is a protected shoreline park near Banyan Drive on Hilo Bay, used for paddling and calm-water recreation.
hazards: Muddy or poor visibility after heavy rain

sources.name: Love Big Island Hilo Beach Guide

464657989.name: Waioli Beach Park
464657989.description: Waioli Beach Park lies along Hanalei Bay by the western part of the bay shoreline.

465331276.name: Black Pot Beach Park
465331276.description: Black Pot Beach Park sits where the Hanalei River enters Hanalei Bay, with shoreline lawns and family picnic areas.
hazards: River currents and water-quality changes after rain

465331284.name: Hanalei Pavilion Beach Park
465331284.description: Hanalei Pavilion Beach Park occupies the central stretch of Hanalei Bay and has a staffed ocean-safety tower.
hazards: High winter surf and rip currents

469797925.name: Alan Davis Beach
469797925.description: Alan Davis Beach, sometimes called Wawamalu or Pele's Chair beach, is a small sandy and rocky area on southeast Oʻahu near the Kaiwi shoreline trail.
amenities: No developed facilities at the beach

471291210.name: Pā'ia Bay Beach
471291210.description: Pāʻia Bay Beach is a north-shore sandy beach close to Pāʻia town, alongside Hāna Highway.

473522966.name: Kaneohe Beach Park
473522966.description: Kāneʻohe Beach Park is a community shoreline park in Kāneʻohe on Oʻahu's windward side, overlooking the bay.
hazards: Shallow muddy or rocky nearshore bottom

sources.name: Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

496362810.name: Kepuhi Beach
496362810.description: Kepuhi Beach is a long sandy beach on the western shore of Molokaʻi, near the former Kaluakoʻi resort area.

500307758.name: Turtle Bay
500307758.description: Turtle Bay is in the Kawela Bay area on Oʻahu, where beach visitors can swim and snorkel and occasionally see sea turtles.

504701462.name: Puuloa Beach Park
504701462.description: Puʻuloa Beach Park is a beach park area on the ʻEwa shoreline of Oʻahu near Pearl Harbor's western approaches.

sources.name: Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

509354370.name: Fort DeRussy Beach Park
509354370.description: Fort DeRussy Beach Park is a section of Waikīkī Beach fronting Fort DeRussy and its beachfront park.

512873129.name: Ukumehame Beach Park
512873129.description: Ukumehame Beach Park is an oceanfront recreation spot on Honoapiʻilani Highway in West Maui, used for picnicking and watersports.

512878189.name: Puamana Beach Park
512878189.description: Puamana Beach Park is a small beachfront park along Honoapiʻilani Highway just south of Lahaina.

532568009.name: Ha'ena Beach
532568009.description: Hāʻena Beach on Hawaiʻi Island is distinct from Hāʻena Beach Park on Kauaʻi; it is a remote Puna coast shoreline with difficult access.

536041576.name: Papakōlea Beach
536041576.description: Papakōlea, also known as Green Sand Beach, is a remote olivine-rich beach near South Point on Hawaiʻi Island.
amenities: No developed facilities at the beach

545382486.name: Diamond Head Beach Park
545382486.description: Tucked beneath dramatic cliffs directly below the Diamond Head Crater; rugged landscape, excellent offshore surf breaks (Lighthouse, Cliffs), and tide pooling. Requires navigating a steep, rocky 80-foot paved access path/switchbacks. Frequently visited by locals and experienced surfers.
hazards: Strong currents, undertows, sharp lava rocks/coral, and hazardous shorebreaks.
Not recommended for beginners or small children.

554993748.name: Ewa Beach Community Park
554993748.description: ʻEwa Beach Community Park is a public community park in ʻEwa Beach; the ocean shoreline is nearby rather than fully within every part of the recreation grounds.
hazards: Nearby open-ocean shore may have strong surf

sources.name: Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

557520582.name: White Sands Beach Park
557520582.description: A popular sandy beach along Aliʻi Drive known for excellent bodyboarding waves. Named "Magic Sands" because winter storms occasionally pull all the sand off the beach overnight, exposing bare lava rock, before summer waves gradually wash the sand back ashore.
hazards: Lifeguarded, but heavy, crashing shorebreaks and intense backwash frequently cause neck and shoulder injuries to swimmers and bodyboarders.

557521081.name: Kahaluu Beach Park
557521081.description: Kahaluʻu Beach Park on the Kona coast is known for its coral reef and abundant reef fish, making it a popular snorkeling location.

559678216.name: Kaimana Beach Park
559678216.description: Kaimana Beach is a sandy beach near the War Memorial Natatorium on Oʻahu, protected in part by an offshore reef. It is a launch point for swimmers and paddlers using Kapua Channel.

583044498.name: Wawaloli Beach Park
583044498.description: Wāwāloli Beach Park lies on the lava-rock coastline close to the Kona airport; its tidal pools and ocean views attract visitors.

583044499.name: Wawaloli Beach
583044499.description: Wāwāloli Beach is a rocky, tide-pool shoreline by the Kona airport, adjacent to Wāwāloli Beach Park.

583044500.name: Ooma Beach
583044500.description: Oʻoma Beach is a narrow shoreline area on the Kona coast near the airport, with sandy and rocky sections.

612829713.name: Isaac Hale Beach Park
612829713.description: Isaac Hale Beach Park, also known as Pohoiki, was reshaped by the 2018 Kīlauea eruption and now includes a black-sand shore and warm ponds.
amenities: ADA-accessible park facilities (not necessarily every beach area)
hazards: Dangerous shorebreak, strong currents and undertow
Natural warm ponds may contain harmful bacteria

sources.name: Hawaiʻi County Parks — Isaac Hale Beach Park

617085377.name: Black Sand Beach
617085377.lifeguard_schedule: Daily, 8:30 AM–5:00 PM (Isaac Hale Beach Park lifeguards; county schedule)
617085377.description: This mapped Black Sand Beach is the volcanic black-sand shore at Pohoiki adjoining Isaac Kepoʻokalani Hale Beach Park in Puna on Hawaiʻi Island. The shore formed during the 2018 Kīlauea eruption and is distinct from Punaluʻu Black Sand Beach.
amenities: Parking and park facilities at adjacent Isaac Hale Beach Park
Park restrooms, picnic pavilion and BBQ grills
Hawaiʻi County lifeguards at the adjacent beach park
hazards: Dangerous shorebreak, rip currents and undertow; ocean swimming can be unsafe
Unstable or shifting volcanic sand and rock along the shore
Warm ocean ponds nearby may present bacterial health hazards

sources.name: Hawaiʻi County Parks — Isaac Hale Beach Park
Go Hawaiʻi — Pohoiki Black Sand Beach

633651201.name: Kaiona Beach Park
633651201.description: Kaiona Beach Park is a small oceanfront park on Oʻahu's windward side east of Waimānalo, near calm reef-protected water in suitable conditions.

sources.name: Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

642005311.name: Kailua Beach
642005311.description: Kailua Beach is a soft-sand windward beach of Kailua Bay with clear water and popular public recreation areas.
amenities: Picnic areas at Kailua Beach Park

643959836.name: Kokololio Beach Park
643959836.description: Kokololio Beach Park is a sandy windward beach park along Kamehameha Highway near Lāʻie on northeast Oʻahu.

sources.name: Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

650319715.name: Kapilina Beach Park
650319715.description: Kapilina Beach Park is a shoreline recreation area near the Kapilina community on Oʻahu's ʻEwa coast.
amenities: Access may depend on current community and public-use rules

670927368.name: Honokowai Beach Park
670927368.description: A narrow, park-lined coastal strip with a shallow, reef-protected pool that breaks most incoming waves, making it popular for toddlers. Located just north of Lahaina in a densely populated condo area.
hazards: The water can be murky and rocky, and the beach is often heavily littered with washed-up seaweed/coral rubble.

671202863.name: Lē'ahi Beach Park
671202863.description: Lēʻahi Beach Park, also known as Diamond Head Beach Park, is a rocky, scenic shoreline below the cliffs of Lēʻahi (Diamond Head).

sources.name: Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

687188253.name: Honl's Beach
687188253.description: Honl's Beach is a small sand-and-lava beach along Aliʻi Drive just south of Kailua-Kona.

727392624.name: Sunset Beach Neighborhood Park
727392624.description: Sunset Beach Neighborhood Park sits behind the wide North Shore beach near the Sunset Beach surf break.
hazards: Very large winter swell and shorebreak

768098899.name: 'Ehukai Beach Park
768098899.description: ʻEhukai Beach Park is the famous North Shore beach beside Banzai Pipeline, facing a shallow reef with very heavy winter surf.
hazards: Extreme winter waves and rip currents

796367657.name: 49 Black Sand Beach
796367657.description: Beautiful white and black sand beach pockets tucked within the Mauna Lani resort footprint, featuring calm snorkeling waters, coral reefs, and sea turtles. Accessed through gated resort community public access parking stalls with registration.
amenities: and parking lots near the resort historic pathways
hazards: Reef structures near shallow entries require cautious footing.

800966841.name: Joe Lukela Beach Park
800966841.description: Joe Lukela Beach Park is a shoreline park on western Oʻahu; local facility and water conditions require confirmation.
hazards: Ocean conditions vary with west-shore swell

802071555.name: Oneula Beach Park
802071555.description: Oneʻula Beach Park is a sandy and rocky beach park on the ʻEwa coast of southwest Oʻahu.

sources.name: Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

808597330.name: Holoholokai Beach Park
808597330.description: Holoholokai Beach Park is a rocky coastal park near Mauna Lani on the Kohala Coast, close to the Puakō Petroglyph Archaeological Preserve.

827891438.name: Nākeikiapua
827891438.description: Nākeikiapua is a mapped coastal beach on northeastern Molokaʻi, a few kilometres east of Honouli Maloʻo Bay Beach and west of Hālawa Bay. Public access and site facilities have not been confirmed.

830516795.name: Kumukea Beach
830516795.description: Kumukea Beach is the sand-and-lava shoreline at the Four Seasons Resort Hualālai in North Kona on Hawaiʻi Island, also described as Kaʻūpūlehu Beach. Public shoreline-access facilities are provided through designated resort access routes.
amenities: Restrooms and showers at the resort shoreline-access area
Nearby resort services may be limited to guests
hazards: Submerged lava rock and uneven footing
Changing surf and currents at rocky shoreline sections
Sea urchins may occur around lava rock

sources.name: Hawaiʻi County Planning — North Kona public shoreline access

842922145.name: Waiehu Beach Park
842922145.description: Waiehu Beach Park is a grassy coastal park on Maui's north shore, with wide ocean views and shoreline access.

856027718.name: Kamilo
856027718.description: Kamilo Beach is a remote shoreline on the island's southeastern Kaʻū coast, widely noted for marine debris that washes ashore.

856103051.name: Kaulahao Beach
856103051.description: Kaulahao Beach is a coastal section in the Pāʻia vicinity of Maui's north shore.

856603197.name: North Beach
856603197.lifeguard_schedule: 11:00 AM–5:30 PM (MCBH posted lifeguard period; confirm current base restrictions)
856603197.description: North Beach is a sandy, surf-exposed beach on Marine Corps Base Hawaiʻi at Kāneʻohe Bay/Mōkapu Peninsula on Oʻahu. Beach access is restricted to eligible military/base personnel and authorized guests; it is not a general-public tourist beach.
amenities: MCBH-managed beach access for authorized patrons
Base lifeguard service during posted hours
hazards: Challenging open-ocean waves and rapidly changing surf conditions
Base flag-system swimming restrictions; often limited to experienced swimmers

886504933.name: Wailupe Beach Park
886504933.description: Wailupe Beach Park is a small shoreline park on southeast Oʻahu near Wailupe and Maunalua Bay.
hazards: Muddy or murky water after rain

sources.name: Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

886585788.name: Nimitz Beach
886585788.description: Nimitz Beach lies on Oʻahu's southwest coastline near Kalaeloa and the former Barbers Point airfield.
amenities: Limited roadside parking or beach access

887587688.name: Kalepolepo Beach Park
887587688.description: Enclosed by an ancient Hawaiian fishpond (loko iʻa) rock wall, creating a shallow, waveless, warm pool that is often calmer than the open shoreline. Located in Kīhei; historically significant site for native aquaculture restoration.
hazards: The water inside the wall can become stagnant with low circulation, and the bottom is muddy/mucky rather than soft sand.

900250532.name: Kahuku Beach
900250532.description: Kahuku Beach is a broad, less developed North Shore shoreline near the Kahuku coastal area.

900782034.name: Laniloa Beach
900782034.description: Lāʻie Nīloa Beach, also called Laniloa Beach, is a sandy windward shoreline near Lāʻie on northeast Oʻahu.
hazards: Strong surf and currents in rough weather

900782040.name: Temple Beach
900782040.description: Temple Beach is a locally used name for a stretch of shoreline near Lāʻie on Oʻahu's northeast coast.
hazards: Strong trade winds and changing surf

900791139.name: Kaʻaʻawa Beach
900791139.description: Kaʻaʻawa Beach is a narrow and scenic windward shoreline on Oʻahu below steep Koʻolau ridges.
hazards: High waves and currents when exposed

900791140.name: Kalaeʻōʻio Beach
900791140.description: Kalaeʻōʻio Beach is a small coastal site near Kualoa and Kaʻaʻawa along windward Oʻahu.

900791142.name: Kahana Bay Beach
900791142.description: Kahana Bay Beach is a curved sandy shore at Kahana Bay on windward Oʻahu, bordered by green mountains.
amenities: Parking at nearby Kahana Bay Beach Park

sources.name: Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

900791152.name: Pounders Beach
900791152.description: Pounders Beach is an exposed sandy shore near Lāʻie on northeast Oʻahu, known for strong shorebreak.

902256344.name: Kaihalulu Beach
